threads.body: The new `code > 0` boundary is not covered for `code == 0`: these cases would still pass if the implementation regressed to `code != 0`, reintroducing the meaningless `"0"` error type. Add a zero-code case to lock down the non-positive fallback behavior.

replies.body: Good call. Added a `code == 0` case: `argumentSet("zero code falls back", new MongoException(0, "boom"), null)`. That pins the exact boundary between `code > 0` and `code >= 0`, so a regression to `code >= 0` (which would reintroduce a `"0"` error type) is now caught. This mirrors the zero-code handling in #19623.
